grammar_focus: Habits and tendencies: tend to, be inclined to, keep (on) -ing, will/would, be always -ing
grammar_html:
• zvyky, fakta, trvalé stavy
I usually start at eight.
děj právě teď, dočasná situace, vývoj
This month I'm starting at seven.

Příslovce frekvence stojí před plnovýznamovým slovesem, ale za slovesem be a za pomocným slovesem: She often works late. × She is often late. × I have never been late.
Výrazy every day, once a week, from time to time stojí obvykle na konci věty.

vocab.ex: I find it hard to stick to a routine when I work from home.
It took me years to break the habit of checking my phone in bed.
During lockdown I fell into the habit of skipping breakfast.
She makes a habit of walking to work every day.
My dad is a creature of habit – he has the same breakfast every day.
I'm an early bird, so I do my best work before nine.
As a night owl, she tends to start working at ten in the evening.
I keep hitting the snooze button and then I'm late.
A weekend in the mountains helps me forget the daily grind.

vocab.cz: rovnováha mezi prací a osobním životem
vocab.ex: Flexible hours have really improved my work-life balance.
Our company offers flexible working hours, so I start at seven.
Half of our team works remotely from different countries.

vocab.en: be up to your eyes in work
vocab.ipa: bi ʌp tə jɔːr aɪz ɪn wɜːk
vocab.ex: Sorry, I can't help – I'm up to my eyes in work.
We worked all weekend to meet the deadline.
He tends to take on extra work and then feels stressed.
The project is running two weeks behind schedule.
Nurses often have to work overtime at weekends.
Let's grab a bite before the meeting.
I usually wind down with a book before bed.
I'm making an effort to go to bed before eleven.
He does the bare minimum and leaves at five on the dot.
However busy she is, she always makes time for her kids.
I felt stuck in a rut, so I changed jobs.
Our receptionist always goes the extra mile for guests.
I had to pull an all-nighter to finish the report.
Students tend to burn the midnight oil before exams.
My colleague showed me the ropes in my first week.

vocab.en: get into the swing of things
vocab.cz: dostat se do tempa, zajet se
vocab.ipa: ɡet ˈɪntə ðə swɪŋ əv θɪŋz
vocab.ex: After the holidays it takes me a few days to get into the swing of things.
We have to clock in by 8.30.
My boss is a stickler for punctuality.
After a month, getting up at six became second nature.

vocab.cz: starých zvyků se člověk těžko zbavuje
vocab.ex: I still write lists on paper – old habits die hard!

exercises.q: She checks her email at 6 a.m. and goes running before work. → (an early bird / be stuck in a rut / go the extra mile / meet a deadline)
The report must be ready by Friday noon and it will be. → (an early bird / be up to your eyes in work / meet a deadline / second nature)
He has done exactly the same job in the same way for twelve years and feels bored. → (an early bird / be stuck in a rut / be up to your eyes in work / hit the snooze button)
She stays in the office until nine to finish things for a client – nobody asked her to. → (be up to your eyes in work / go the extra mile / hit the snooze button / second nature)
He has fourteen projects and no free minute this week. → (be up to your eyes in work / do the bare minimum / go the extra mile / meet a deadline)
exercises.a: be up to your eyes in work

exercises.q: Every morning I press the button on my alarm clock three times. → (be stuck in a rut / do the bare minimum / hit the snooze button / meet a deadline)
After a month in the new job, using the system is automatic for me. → (be stuck in a rut / do the bare minimum / go the extra mile / second nature)
He never does more than he absolutely has to. → (an early bird / do the bare minimum / hit the snooze button / second nature)
I (usually walk / am usually walking) to work, but this week I'm taking the tram.
I usually walk to work, but this week I (take / 'm taking) the tram.
Our team (grows / is growing) fast – we have three new colleagues this month.
She (is never / never is) late for meetings.
Why (do you wear / are you wearing) a suit today? Have you got an interview?
My boss (doesn't believe / isn't believing) in working from home.
I (hardly ever eat / eat hardly ever) breakfast on weekdays.
I check my email before breakfast. (always)
exercises.a: I always check my email before breakfast.

exercises.q: He is in the office on Fridays. (rarely)
exercises.a: He is rarely in the office on Fridays.

exercises.q: We have lunch together. (once a week)
exercises.a: We have lunch together once a week.

exercises.q: Do you work at weekends? (ever)
exercises.a: Do you ever work at weekends?

exercises.q: They have missed a deadline. (never)
exercises.a: They have never missed a deadline.

exercises.q: I (tend to / am tending to) get up later at weekends.
My colleague (is always borrowing / always borrows) my stapler without asking – it drives me crazy!
When I was a student, I (would / will) work in a café every summer.
I (keep making / keep to make) the same mistake in my reports.
When I lived in London, I (would have / used to have) a two-hour commute.
Our manager (is inclined to / inclines to) change her mind at the last minute.
People who work remotely (tend not to / don't tend) take enough breaks.
My dad (will / would) always read the newspaper before he talks to anyone in the morning – he still does it.
I usually feel tired after lunch. (tend)
exercises.a: I tend to feel tired after lunch.

exercises.q: He forgets his ID card again and again. (keep)
exercises.a: He keeps forgetting his ID card. | He keeps on forgetting his ID card.

exercises.q: As a child, I often hid under the table when guests came. (would)
exercises.a: As a child, I would hide under the table when guests came.

exercises.q: She leaves dirty cups in the sink all the time and it annoys me. (always)
exercises.a: She's always leaving dirty cups in the sink. | She is always leaving dirty cups in the sink.

exercises.q: Petr often gets angry when he's tired. (inclined)
exercises.a: Petr is inclined to get angry when he's tired.

exercises.q: We don't usually work late on Fridays. (tend)
exercises.a: We don't tend to work late on Fridays. | We tend not to work late on Fridays.

exercises.q: I'm really trying to ______ an effort to leave the office on time.
He just ______ the bare minimum and never volunteers for anything.
Could you ______ me a favour and send this file to the client?
She ______ a habit of reading for twenty minutes before bed.
We need to ______ some research before we ______ a decision.
However busy you are, you should ______ time for your family.
I'm ______ overtime this week to finish the project.
Our new intern is ______ great progress.
I'm tending to drink too much coffee at work.
exercises.a: I tend to drink too much coffee at work.

exercises.q: He keeps to forget his keys.
When I was young, I would live in a small village.
exercises.a: When I was young, I used to live in a small village.

exercises.q: She always is complaining about her boss.
exercises.a: She is always complaining about her boss.

exercises.q: We didn't meet the deadline because we did a lot of mistakes.
exercises.a: We didn't meet the deadline because we made a lot of mistakes.

exercises.q: I'm up to my eye in work this week.
exercises.a: I'm up to my eyes in work this week.

exercises.q: I (tend to / am tending to) work better in the morning.
He (keeps forgetting / keeps to forget) his badge.
My sister (is always borrowing / always borrows) my clothes – it's so annoying!
As a student, I (would / will) cycle to university every day.
We (used to / would) have an office in the city centre.
She (is inclined to / is inclining to) work too hard.
I need to (make / do) an effort to go to bed earlier.
He only (does / makes) the bare minimum.
The project is running behind (schedule / timetable).
I'm up to my (eyes / ears) in work.
I (usually start / am usually starting) at eight, but this week I'm starting at seven.
I usually start at eight, but this week I (start / 'm starting) at seven.
She (is never / never is) late.
I keep _____ (hit) the snooze button.
We don't _____ to work late on Fridays.
He _____ always leaving his cup on my desk!
I find it hard to stick _____ a routine.
Flexible hours improved my work-life _____.
We worked all night to _____ the deadline.
tends / she / to / late / work
always / he / is / complaining
keep / I / my / forgetting / password
